captions.detailed: This 3D model is a parametric pencil clip designed for holding a standard hexagonal pencil and clipping onto a flat surface like a notebook cover. It features a main cylindrical sleeve with a hexagonal cutout sized for a pencil, connected to a flat, double-walled clip body. The far end of the clip terminates in two rounded cylinder grips that squeeze together. The entire model is vertically extruded with a uniform height.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric pencil clip in OpenSCAD that holds a standard hexagonal pencil. It should feature an adjustable pencil radius, wall thickness, overall height, and clip length, utilizing a hexagonal cutout for the pencil grip and including rounded cylindrical ends at the open side of the clip.
captions.factory: The model uses a difference() operation to subtract a hexagonal cavity (using the MCAD hexagon module) from a main outer cylinder representing the pencil sleeve. This sleeve is unioned with two parallel flat plates (using cube primitives) that form the clip body. The texturing on the plates is done using write.scad. At the open end of the clip, two small cylinders are translated and attached to the plates to form soft, rounded gripping edges.
